newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Endesa tries to diversify before sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Endesa tries to diversify before sell-off.

text.p: Spanish electricity group Endesa's bid for Sevillana and Fecsa is an attempt to lessen the blow of planned deregulation in the sector prior to the public company's privatisation, analysts said on Friday.

"Endesa is trying to gain market share in distribution, as the planned deregulation of the sector will affect its principal activity, the generation of electricity," said an analyst at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
The government announced on Monday that it planned to sell off part of its 66-percent stake in Endesa.

Spain's Stock Market Commission (CMMV) said on Friday that Endesa was launching a bid for up to 75 percent of Fecsa at 1,100 pesetas ($8.47) a share and for up to 75 percent of Sevillana at 1,300 pesetas a share.
Sevillana's board has announced that it is recommending that shareholders accept the offer. Endesa already holds a 39.4 percent stake in Sevillana and a 49 percent stake in Fecsa.
Control of the regional electricity companies would help expand Endesa's current 20 percent share of the distribution market, analysts said.
Planned deregulation of the market is expected to slash the profitability of Endesa's electricity generation business.
Analysts said Sevillana would be an attractive addition to Endesa's operations, as it was a financially healthy company and controlled the lucrative Maghreb gas pipeline.
Although Fecsa's financial state was less attractive, analysts highlighted its hydraulic power assets and its Catalan market.

"Endesa is trying to diversify its operations and gain a hold in distribution. If it merges both subsidiaries it will achieve a reduction in costs," said Fabian Ramon at the Financial Savings Corporation.
However market sources said Endesa's strategy illustrated that shareholders were taking second place.
"Endesa is always buying expensively, and now its share price will suffer with two takeovers," said one market source.
But shares in Endesa climbed after trade resumed on Friday, opening at 8,100 pesetas compared with Thursday's close of 7,950 pesetas.
Shares in Sevillana and Endesa also advanced. Sevillana resumed trading at 1,255, up 7.7 percent on Thursday's close. Fecsa was up seven percent at 1,070.

Analysts warned that the deal could involve political complications. The Andalusian and Catalan regional government are both thought to be reluctant to allow the electricity companies lose their regional identity.
"There are conflicting interests. It is not a decision that can be taken solely from the economic-financial point of view," said Fabian Ramon from the Financial Saving Corporation.
